balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Magellan Financial Group Limited (renaming to Barrenjoey Group Limited, ASX: BJY, subject to October 2026 AGM approval): equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Magellan Financial Group Limited (renaming to Barrenjoey Group Limited, ASX: BJY, subject to October 2026 AGM approval): the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Magellan Financial Group Limited (renaming to Barrenjoey Group Limited, ASX: BJY, subject to October 2026 AGM approval): the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Magellan Financial Group Limited (renaming to Barrenjoey Group Limited, ASX: BJY, subject to October 2026 AGM approval): the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Magellan Financial Group Limited (renaming to Barrenjoey Group Limited, ASX: BJY, subject to October 2026 AGM approval): the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Magellan Financial Group Limited (renaming to Barrenjoey Group Limited, ASX: BJY, subject to October 2026 AGM approval): CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Statutory net income vs operating profit
profit.content:
Net income (statutory) is the audited bottom line after all one-off items. Operating profit is Magellan's own non-IFRS headline measure, adding back items management treats as non-recurring (e.g. Barrenjoey-related transaction costs, impairments on the heritage funds outsourcing to Vinva).

For Magellan Financial Group Limited (renaming to Barrenjoey Group Limited, ASX: BJY, subject to October 2026 AGM approval): FY2026 statutory NPAT was A$87.9m (down 47% YoY) versus operating profit after tax of A$144.9m (down only 9%) -- a A$57m gap driven by the one-off costs of the Global Equities repositioning and Barrenjoey merger. Use operating profit for the run-rate trend, but never ignore the statutory number: it is what shareholders' equity actually moves by.

What to watch:

  • The size of the statutory/operating gap -- a widening gap means more of "underlying" earnings is being adjusted away
  • Whether items management calls one-off (transaction costs) keep recurring year after year

fumFees.title: Average FUM vs fee revenue
fumFees.content:
Average funds under management (FUM) is the fee-earning asset base a fund manager is paid on; management fees are the recurring revenue line (average FUM × the base fee rate), and performance fees are the volatile, outperformance-linked top-up.

For Magellan Financial Group Limited (renaming to Barrenjoey Group Limited, ASX: BJY, subject to October 2026 AGM approval): this is the core narrative of the business. Average FUM peaked at A$113.9bn in FY2021 and has since collapsed to A$36-40bn (Hamish Douglass's 2021-22 departure, sustained investment underperformance and client redemptions), taking management fees from over A$700m to roughly A$200m. Performance fees have been near zero since FY2023 -- there is little outperformance left to be paid on. The FY2026 outsourcing of the heritage Global Equities funds to Vinva and the closure of the currency-hedged fund shrink the FUM base further before any Barrenjoey diversification offsets it.

What to watch:

  • Whether average FUM stabilises or keeps declining -- it is the leading indicator, fee revenue lags it by a period
  • Net flows (redemptions vs inflows) versus market-driven FUM moves
  • Performance fees returning would signal a genuine investment turnaround, not just cost cuts

feeBps.title: Average base management fee rate
feeBps.content:
The average base management fee, in basis points (bps, hundredths of a percent) of average FUM, is the price Magellan charges for managing money before any performance fee. It is separate from the FUM/fee chart because a fund manager's fee revenue can fall for two independent reasons -- less money to manage, or a lower price charged on the money it still has -- and this isolates the second.

For Magellan Financial Group Limited (renaming to Barrenjoey Group Limited, ASX: BJY, subject to October 2026 AGM approval): the base fee rate has compressed from 66bps (FY2017) to 52bps (FY2026), and management's FY2026 repricing of the heritage Global Equities funds as part of the Vinva handover will push it lower still in FY2027. Fee compression means management fee revenue falls faster than FUM itself -- the FUM chart alone understates the revenue pressure.

What to watch:

  • Further step-downs disclosed around fund repricing or new lower-cost mandates
  • Mix shift toward lower-fee institutional/systematic mandates (e.g. Vinva Systematic Equities) versus higher-fee retail funds

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Magellan Financial Group Limited (renaming to Barrenjoey Group Limited, ASX: BJY, subject to October 2026 AGM approval): the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Magellan Financial Group Limited (renaming to Barrenjoey Group Limited, ASX: BJY, subject to October 2026 AGM approval): the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
